facts.raw_span: 1 week of difficulty voiding
was catheterized for urinary retention
a large prostatic mass
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.62 ng/mL
he denied pain, fever, or abdominal distension
Physical examination was unremarkable

a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe
cystoscopy raised suspicion for bladder invasion
Positron emission tomography–CT and colonoscopy suggested rectal invasion

rationales.F01: Difficulty voiding is a common symptom of prostatic conditions
rationales.F02: Urinary retention is a common complication of prostatic conditions
rationales.F03: A large prostatic mass is a characteristic finding of prostatic sarcoma and stromal tumors
rationales.F04: A low prostate-specific antigen level is less typical of prostatic sarcoma
rationales.F08: An enlarged prostate with palpable nodules is a characteristic finding of prostatic conditions
rationales.F09: A heterogeneous lesion in the prostate is a characteristic finding of prostatic sarcoma and stromal tumors
rationales.F10: Bladder invasion is more typical of prostatic sarcoma
rationales.F11: Rectal invasion is more typical of prostatic sarcoma
rationales.F12: The biopsy result is highly suggestive of prostatic stromal sarcoma or stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential

frontier_selector.runner_up: Prostatic Stromal Tumor of Uncertain Malignant Potential
frontier_selector.why: The evidence of a large prostatic mass and a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe, along with the biopsy result indicating prostatic stromal sarcoma or prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential, decided it, leaning towards the more specific and severe diagnosis of Prostatic Stromal Sarcoma due to the presence of a significant mass and lesion size.
